turns.content: I'm on a salary of NGN 2,400,000 a year and I've never claimed any relief. What might I be missing?

Let's find out. What do you pay in rent each year? Do you make pension contributions beyond the mandatory ones, and do you have NHF, NHIS, a life insurance policy, or a mortgage on a home you live in?
I pay NGN 3,000,000 in rent a year. I can also increase my pension - what would that save me in tax?

With your NGN 3,000,000 rent claimed, rent relief is NGN 500,000 (the cap) and your tax would be NGN 165,000. If you increase your pension by NGN 120,000, the tax drops to NGN 147,000 - a saving of NGN 18,000, because that amount comes off income taxed at 15%. Keep the rent documents and your RSA statement for the claims.
I earn NGN 100,000,000 a year and I currently contribute NGN 1,200,000 to pension. If I increase that to NGN 1,320,000, how much tax do I save?

With NGN 1,200,000 of pension your tax is NGN 22,630,000. Increasing to NGN 1,320,000 - an extra NGN 120,000 - brings the tax to NGN 22,600,000. Saving: NGN 30,000, because the extra comes off your 25% band.
Is there a limit on how much I can contribute voluntarily?

Yes: a voluntary contribution must come from legitimate income and be no more than one-third of your month's salary, made once a month. You notify your employer in writing and the employer remits it to your RSA.
I have some spare savings this year on a NGN 60,000,000 salary. What should I prioritise for tax?

Voluntary pension first - it's the lever you control, and contributions are deductible. After that, confirm any rent, NHF, NHIS, life insurance or mortgage interest you already pay is claimed with evidence.
How do I set up the voluntary pension?
Decide the monthly amount (no more than one-third of your month's salary), notify your employer in writing, and they remit it to your RSA through your PFA - contributions go once a month.
If I increase my pension to NGN 1,320,000 from NGN 1,200,000, how much tax do I save?
Your tax with NGN 1,200,000 of pension is NGN 12,630,000. At NGN 1,320,000 it drops to NGN 12,600,000 - NGN 30,000 saved, because the extra NGN 120,000 leaves your 25% band.
I earn NGN 18,000,000 a year and I rent my flat, but I've never claimed anything. What am I missing?

Quite possibly a few things. What do you pay in rent per year? Any NHF or NHIS contributions, a life insurance policy, or interest on a mortgage for a home you live in? And you can add voluntary pension on top of the mandatory contribution.
I pay NGN 600,000 rent a year, and I can add NGN 120,000 to my pension. What would that save?

With rent relief of NGN 120,000 (20% of your NGN 600,000 rent) your tax is NGN 3,184,800. Adding NGN 120,000 of pension lowers it to NGN 3,159,600 - a saving of NGN 25,200, since it comes off the 21% band. Claim the rent in writing and keep the receipts.

With NGN 240,000 of pension your tax is NGN 610,800. At NGN 360,000 it becomes NGN 589,200 - NGN 21,600 saved, because the extra NGN 120,000 comes off income taxed at 18%.

Voluntary contributions are capped at one-third of your month's salary, made once a month, through your employer - notify them in writing of the amount.
